description: Institutions lose authority funding legitimacy and coordination capacity across multiple global domains.
Climate biodiversity health food and disaster crises overwhelm ordinary governance systems.
Competing blocs institutions standards payment systems and technology regimes weaken global public goods.
Private digital financial supply-chain and AI infrastructures govern public life without enough accountability.
Expert and technical systems coordinate decisions but fail to earn public trust or participation.
Regional governance improves some areas while vulnerable states and communities remain underprotected.
Reform commitments fail to secure finance representation and implementation.
Strong legitimacy goals are weakened by implementation constraints and political resistance.
